raw_response:
I’m an old farmer, I don’t count things like the experts do. I look at what my land did before, what the neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can really put out. This year I’ll keep the same pattern mostly steady. On the better 8 mu I’ll do wheat and then summer maize right after, because that gives grain and cash both, and it spreads the risk. The other 6 mu I’ll keep in cotton. Cotton takes more picking, but I’ve grown it many years and I know how to manage it. Fertilizer is expensive, water from the well also costs money, so I won’t push too hard. I’d rather use a steady amount, not too little, not too much, and save some cash in case the weather turns bad or we need to hire help.

For wheat, I’ll sow in early October like we always do. I’ll use ordinary local seed I can get nearby, put on base fertilizer before sowing, then give another bit when the crop starts standing up strong in spring. I’ll water around sowing if the soil is dry, then again at jointing and maybe once at filling if there’s no rain. As soon as wheat comes off in June, I won’t waste time. The maize has to go in fast on the same 8 mu, maybe with light tillage or direct planting if I can get the machine in time. For cotton, I’ll stay moderate. Cotton can make money, but it eats labor, especially picking, and my family is not all at home, so I won’t expand it.
